reason: The goal calls for connecting the switch harness to the rover.

reaction: The new lines make the connection visible.

effect: The pen carriage is on the rover's guides; the return spring is next.
reaction: The bracket between the two rods makes its placement clear.
reason: The spring should slide onto the rover's pen assembly, as the goal directs.

effect: The spring is fitted around one guide rod; the guide cap is next.
reaction: Its position beside the carriage is clear.
reason: The goal directs me to press the guide cap onto the rover assembly.
expectation: The cap will attach to the guides.

effect: The guide cap completed the drawing rover, whose motion shows it turning over a circular line.
reaction: Seeing the assembled rover move and leave a line is a satisfying payoff.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the pen carriage was worthwhile because its position between the guide rods made the drawing mechanism easier to understand.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the two guards felt somewhat repetitive, though the second exposed box made the sequence clear.

surprise.text: The completed rover turns and shows a circular line beneath it, revealing what the pen assembly is for.

arbitrary.text: Choosing which guard to fit first felt like a guess; the goal did not distinguish them.

continue.text: I would continue to see another mechanism take shape, although this chapter's instructions left few meaningful choices.
